newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo Car to continue cost cuts in '97.
newsitem.headline: Volvo Car to continue cost cuts in '97.

text.p: The car unit of Swedish vehicle maker AB Volvo will continue to cut costs in 1997 with costs per car estimated to fall by 5,000 crowns within the next 12 months, the company said on Thursday.
"We will continue our focus on cost reductions," said Volvo Car's managing director Tuve Johannesson at company seminar.
He said a large part of the savings would come from improvements in Volvo's product line.
The successful move from the 850 model to the S/V70 was a good example of that, he said.
"We are looking to reduce costs at the same time as raising prices for our products," Johannesson said.
"We are selling our models at a higher price which increases our profitablity."
Volvo Cars will also reach its sales target of 100,000-110,000 S/V40 in 1997, Johannesson said.
He said Volvo will present an "exciting" new launch in the week of June 23.
